subject: A Research method question and its implementation in Lavaan

messages.author: 9ab2460787fc70a3
messages.subject: A Research method question and its implementation in Lavaan
parts:
Hi,

I am planning to test a hypothesis that is formulated like this:

Among respondents who have high x (independent), those with high Y (independent) will have higher z (dependent) variable.

What would be the best approach for testing such hypothesis in Lavaan? Should I define a new pseudo variable that is made from multiplication of the two independent variables in my model?

Thank you

messages.author: bfa43814f6ba1969
messages.subject: Re: A Research method question and its implementation in Lavaan
parts:
Hi,

If you are working with observed variables, that is the way to go. See e.g.

Dawson, J. F. (2014). Moderation in Management Research: What, Why, When, and How. Journal of Business and Psychology, 29(1), 1–19. https://doi.org/10.1007/s10869-013-9308-7

If you have moderation between latent variables, then things get a bit more trickier. I recommend taking a look at Kline’s book first.

Kline, R. B. (2011). Principles and practice of structural equation modeling (3rd ed.). New York, NY: Guilford Press.

Mikko
